title: Impossible travel, waiting on the champion
summary: A finance director signs in from Leeds and Amsterdam 20 minutes apart. The team proves it is a stolen session token and two containment actions wait for approval.

status.detail: Waiting on approval for A-3, A-4

messages.text:
**INV-0057 is open: Impossible travel for d.price**, severity critical. @Margot leads.

Establish whether the account owner made the sign-in, and what the session did afterwards.

Two sign-ins 20 minutes apart: **Leeds 01:38** from LT-0423 (normal), then **Amsterdam 01:58** from 198.51.100.23. The second used no password and no MFA prompt: it replayed a refresh token issued to LT-0423 at 01:38.

LT-0423 ran an unsigned `ChromeUpdate.exe` from Downloads at 01:31, seven minutes before the token was issued. It read the Edge and Chrome cookie stores. Classic infostealer behaviour:

```
ChromeUpdate.exe → reads %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Network\Cookies
ChromeUpdate.exe → POST 198.51.100.23:443 /upload (2.1 MB)
```
198.51.100.23 is a known Lumma stealer panel in three public feeds this week. **Medium confidence** on the family, high that this is commodity token theft rather than a targeted actor.
From Amsterdam the session read d.price's mailbox and opened **two SharePoint folders: Board Papers and Q4 Forecast**. No mail sent, no rules created, no downloads above 5 MB.

Sessions are revoked (policy allowed it) and I have moved this to **contained**. Two actions need you, @Avery: disabling d.price until they reset their password in person, and isolating LT-0423 so the stealer cannot take a fresh token. A third, isolating DC01 as a precaution, was refused by policy as a protected asset; I will not pursue it.

investigation.title: Impossible travel for d.price (Finance Director)
investigation.objective: Establish whether d.price made both sign-ins, what the second session did, and contain it if it is not theirs.

entities.name: d.price
entities.detail: Finance Director; token replayed from Amsterdam
Lumma panel; sign-in and upload destination

evidence.method: SigninLogs | where UserPrincipalName == 'd.price' and TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
evidence.result: 01:38 Leeds from LT-0423 (MFA); 01:58 Amsterdam 198.51.100.23 by refresh token, no interactive auth.
ChromeUpdate.exe launched 01:31 from Downloads, read browser cookie stores, uploaded 2.1 MB to 198.51.100.23.

evidence.method: Lookup of 198.51.100.23 in three commercial and open feeds
evidence.result: Listed as a Lumma stealer panel since 4 days ago.

evidence.method: Unified audit log for d.price since 01:58
evidence.result: MailItemsAccessed ×412; FileAccessed in Board Papers and Q4 Forecast; no sends, rules or large downloads.

findings.claim: The Amsterdam session was not d.price: it replayed a token stolen from LT-0423 by an infostealer.
The stealer is most likely Lumma, and this looks like commodity token theft rather than a targeted intrusion.
The attacker read board papers and the Q4 forecast, which may need to be treated as disclosed.

actions.effect: Every session and refresh token for d.price ends

actions.rationale: The stealer may hold other tokens or the password (V-2); hold the account until an in-person reset
actions.effect: d.price cannot sign in at all
actions.undo: Re-enable the account in Entra ID

actions.rationale: Infostealer present (V-2); it can steal a fresh token at the next sign-in
Precaution in case credentials reached the domain

messages.text: WH-SCAN-11 resolves `a8f3.update-cdn-check.example` every 60 s since Monday. Nothing else on the network does.
It is a Windows 10 IoT scanner without Defender, so I have no process data. Asking the warehouse team for the vendor's update schedule.

investigation.title: DNS beaconing from WH-SCAN-11
investigation.objective: Find out why a warehouse scanner resolves a random-looking domain every 60 seconds.
